title: flex-wrap
definition: A flexbox container property that specifies whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines.
simpleExplanation: By default, Flexbox is stubborn. If you put 10 boxes into a container, it will squeeze and crush them until they fit on a single line. Setting `flex-wrap: wrap` tells the browser: 'If there isn't enough room, it's okay, drop the extra boxes down to a new row'.
realWorldExample: An image gallery. You want 4 images per row on a Desktop, but on a Mobile phone, they should automatically wrap to form 1 image per row.
useCases: Responsive lists of cards that stack on mobile

basic: What is the default value of `flex-wrap`?
intermediate: If items wrap to a second line, how do you control the vertical space between the two lines?

answers.question: Default value?
answers.answer: `nowrap`. Items will shrink infinitely to stay on one line.

answers.question: Space between lines?
answers.answer: You can use `gap: 20px;` on the flex container, which creates a grid-like gutter between both columns AND rows.

codeExample:
Resize your browser window slowly. Watch the orange boxes drop to a new line when they run out of room!
